description: We are building "Radio Silence", a browser game for kids (8-12) where you run a small Moon outpost and balance power, oxygen, food and radiation safety. Our twist: Mission Control replies arrive late, so players must decide on their own, and at the end the game compares their choices with what NASA really did in a real mission.
summary: Radio Silence is a browser game for kids aged 8 to 12 that trains them to run a small Moon outpost. Players balance power, oxygen, food and radiation safety, then face a crisis based on NASA's real Apollo 13 mission. Mission Control's reply arrives late, so players learn why astronauts must be ready to decide on their own. It answers the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge by turning real mission lessons into short, playable decisions.
details:
What it does: Players survive 10 sols (Moon days). Each sol they get two moves. Every move helps one system and costs another, for example grow lights give food but use power. On sol 4, a crisis based on Apollo 13 hits. The player can send one message to Mission Control, but the reply takes 3 sols (a game rule, not real radio timing). The reply unlocks a "Build CO2 adapter" move inspired by the real improvised fix. If the player asks too late, the reply arrives after the mission ends. The end screen compares "What you did" with "What NASA did" and links to NASA sources.

How it works: A static web game built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no server needed. Game data (meters, actions, crisis, debrief) lives in separate files so the research teammate can update facts without touching game code. We tested difficulty with simple simulations so the game is challenging but winnable.

Benefits: Kids practise trade-offs and planning, and learn why crews need to act without instant help from Earth.

Note: All game numbers are gameplay estimates, not NASA engineering specifications.

Goal: Add more real missions (such as the 1972 solar storm) and a classroom mode.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Figma, GitHub, Node.js (data tests).
